## Goal
Explore and understand the Spotify API documentation, with a focus on music player queue management and authentication endpoints.

## Constraints & Preferences
- (none)

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Retrieved list of all available apps and their descriptions
- [x] Retrieved full list of Spotify API endpoints
- [x] Examined `show_song_queue` API doc (GET `/music_player/song_queue`)
- [x] Examined `show_liked_songs` API doc (GET `/liked_songs`)
- [x] Examined `remove_song_from_queue` API doc (DELETE `/music_player/song_queue/{position}`)
- [x] Examined `play_music` API doc (POST `/music_player/play`)
- [x] Examined `login` API doc (POST `/auth/token`)

## Key Decisions
- **Focus on Spotify music player APIs**: The assistant chose to deep-dive into queue-related endpoints after reviewing all available apps.

## Next Steps
1. Determine the actual task or operation the user wants to perform with Spotify
2. If needed, authenticate using `login` (POST `/auth/token`) with username and password to obtain `access_token`
3. Use `show_song_queue` to inspect current queue state
4. Perform desired queue operations (e.g., `remove_song_from_queue`, `play_music`) using the access token

## Critical Context
- Spotify `login` requires `username` (email) and `password`; returns `access_token` and `token_type`
- `show_song_queue` returns queue songs with fields: `song_id`, `title`, `album_id`, `album_title`, `duration`, `artists`, `position`, `is_playing`, `is_current`
- `remove_song_from_queue` requires `position` (0-indexed) and `access_token`
- `play_music` accepts at most one of: `queue_position`, `song_id`, `album_id`, `playlist_id`
- `show_liked_songs` supports pagination (`page_index`, `page_limit`) and sorting by `liked_at`, `play_count`, `title` (default: `-liked_at`)
